newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Williams sells 15 businesses in MBO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Williams sells 15 businesses in MBO.

text.p: International manufacturing group Williams Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it was selling 15 heating, construction and home products units in a management buyout in order to concentrate on its key businesses.
Williams is selling the mainly British-orientated businesses to a management buyout (MBO) group for 360 million pounds ($600.5 million) in cash.

Williams will retain a 26 percent stake in the buyout company, which will be called Newmond Ltd and covers activities including the Swish curtain track business and Rawlplug construction and home improvement products.

"This sale clearly demonstrates our commitment to focusing on businesses with international growth potential. The proceeds will provide the group with substantial additional resources with which to strengthen and develop our international positions in fire protection, security products and home improvement products," chairman Sir Nigel Rudd said in a statement.

"We have been developing the consistently narrowing focus of Williams," chief executive Roger Carr said in an interview. He said the deal also demonstrated the company was adding value for shareholders.
Net cash inflow of 303 million pounds from the deal leaves Williams with zero net debt and in a position to pursue acquisitions in its three main areas.

Carr said the company, which as an international manufacturing group has sought to shrug off the image of a conglomerate, had a number of acquisition opportunities in mind, "some of which we are looking at seriously."
The company, which has spent 230 million pounds on nine acquisitions this year, had looked at opportunites in the Far East, Europe and North America.
"Relevance is the key rather than size -- we have three good divisions which we will build on," Carr said.

The stock market reacted positively to the deal and Williams shares rose by 6-1/2 pence to 346. "It's a buy' from these levels," said Andrew Crispin of Societe Generale, adding that a trading update from Williams confirmed expected trends.
On current trading, Williams said favourable conditions had continued in the U.S. and there was some improvement in Britain, but European markets remained difficult.
Carr warned about the strength of the pound, but said management action meant the impact had been very limited this year.
Williams expects to make an exceptional gain of some 246 million pounds on the sale and, after deducting goodwill, the deal represents a net balance sheet gain of 90 million pounds.
Carr said that on Williams' calculations the businesses had delivered a return of 13 percent since their various acquisitions, ahead of the cost of capital.

He said Williams' group target for rate of return was 12 to 15 percent. "If you can achieve that you are doing pretty well in the economic environment -- and you never expose the full value until you sell the businesses," he said.
Williams is reinvesting 57 million pounds to take its 26 percent stake in the buyout company, which Carr said was led by a "highly-respected management team".
The MBO will be led by Mike Davies, who will resign as a director of Williams, and is in partnership with Candover Partners Ltd. ($1=.5995 Pound)
